newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin opposes NATO membership for CIS states.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin opposes NATO membership for CIS states.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin said on Friday Russia wanted NATO to abandon any idea of integrating former Soviet republics into the Western defence alliance, Interfax news agency said.

Yeltsin, speaking to Russian media chiefs, made clear that this was a condition for Moscow as it negotiates an agreement with NATO mapping out their future relations. He singled out the three Baltic former Soviet republics for specific mention.
Yeltsin said Russia would not make any concessions at a summit with U.S. President Bill Clinton in Helsinki next week that threatened its defence capability. He gave no details.
"Our other categoric condition is that NATO does not in any form draw in the countries of the Baltics and the CIS (Commonwealth of Independent States)," Yeltsin said.

"In connection with this, the Russian leadership is alarmed by contacts between NATO and the leaderships of these countries, including the trip by alliance Secretary-General Javier Solana to a series of CIS states."

Solana has in recent weeks visited several members of the loose CIS, which includes all former Soviet republics except Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia. Russia, which opposes NATO's plans to expand eastwards, particularly fears the security implications if CIS member states join the alliance.
